co_blodgett_peak.blurb: Blodgett Peak rises above the northwest edge of Colorado Springs, with its lower slopes in a city open space and the summit in national forest. Bouldering is the main reason to come: well over a hundred problems are scattered across the hillsides and a side canyon, from easy to very hard. Roped climbing is a smaller affair, a few trad lines on the East Face and a mix of sport and trad at Skyline Crag, mostly between 5.6 and 5.12 with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. Expect a steep, sustained uphill hike of roughly 45 to 60 minutes to reach the rock, so it suits fit climbers who want quiet.

co_lower_great_face.blurb: Lower Great Face is a broad, low-angle wall on the west side of Twin Sisters, south of Estes Park near Lily Lake, and part of The Crags. A blunt buttress splits it into sections, with the Wizard's Gate sector the busiest for bolted lines. Routes run from short pitches up to about four or five pitches, and the rock is rough with plenty of edges, flakes and corners. Climbs here split fairly evenly between sport and trad, nearly all between 5.8 and 5.10, with one easier line and one 5.11. The walk in is steep and takes around 45 minutes to an hour, and the path can be hard to follow, so it rewards a patient start.

co_spiral_staircase_area.blurb: Spiral Staircase is a compact ice and mixed zone near East Vail, around 9,000 feet, set above the Rigid Designator amphitheatre. Pitches are short, under roughly 25 metres, which keeps it popular with people building skills. The namesake flow is a well-travelled slab of ice that often feels easier than its grade, and lines have been added on either side and in an upper bowl packed with modern mixed climbs. Most of the seventeen climbs are water ice, mainly WI4 and WI5, with a handful of mixed pitches from moderate to hard.

co_seal_rock_climbs.blurb: Seal Rock stands out among the Flatirons, perched high on Bear Canyon's southern slope above Boulder, its north face streaked yellow and orange. The climbing splits by side. The east face holds a few mellow, multi-pitch 5.4 trad routes on slab. The north and south faces carry bolted sport lines, with the south face steeply overhanging and hosting the hardest routes. Roughly two thirds of the seventeen routes are sport, and many of them sit at 5.13 and 5.14, with a smaller group from 5.9 to 5.12. The walk in is a steady uphill hike along the Mesa Trail and a side path.
